'Verify that AI Actors responsible for monitoring reported issues can effectively evaluate GAI system performance ... and promptly escalate issues for response'; owners have recorded response targets. [AI 600-1 p.45]

'Feedback processes for end users and impacted communities to report problems ... are established'; E-04 routes user reports of suspicious agent behavior to a named owner with a response target. [AI 100-1 Table 3 p.31]

'Establish and maintain policies and procedures to record and track GAI system reported errors, near-misses, and negative impacts'; E-04 denial signals are near-miss records, routed to owners with response targets. [AI 600-1 p.45]

E-05.justification: Behavior of the system and its components is monitored in production against per-agent baselines. [AI 100-1 Table 3 p.29]

Mechanisms 'to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use'; E-05 throttles or suspends automatically at the narrowest scope. [AI 100-1 Table 4 p.32]
'Appropriateness of AI metrics and effectiveness of existing controls are regularly assessed'; false-positive rates are recorded. [AI 100-1 Table 3 p.29]
'Verify that GAI system architecture can monitor outputs and performance, and handle, recover from, and repair errors when security anomalies, threats and impacts are detected'. [AI 600-1 p.32]
'Establish and regularly review specific criteria that warrants the deactivation of GAI systems'; recorded thresholds for automatic containment. [AI 600-1 p.42]

E-06.justification: 'Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems'; E-06 lets operators stop a run with its descendants and disable tools, components, model versions or agents without a deploy. Assigning responsibilities is organizational. [AI 100-1 Table 4 p.32]

'procedures for escalating GAI system incidents to the organizational risk management authority when specific criteria for deactivation or disengagement is met'; E-06 provides the mechanism such procedures invoke. [AI 600-1 p.42]
'specific criteria that warrants the deactivation of GAI systems'; E-06 makes deactivation at component granularity possible once criteria are met. [AI 600-1 p.42]

E-07.justification: Deactivation mechanisms at tenant and global scope, with credential revocation and cancellation of queued and descendant work. [AI 100-1 Table 4 p.32]
Safety metrics reflect 'response times for AI system failures'; E-07 measures revocation latency per scope. [AI 100-1 Table 3 p.30]
Deactivation criteria; E-07 provides the scopes at which deactivation can be applied. [AI 600-1 p.42]

E-08.justification: 'Procedures are followed to respond to and recover from a previously unknown risk when it is identified'; quarantine, purge by lineage and restore from a trusted baseline. [AI 100-1 Table 4 p.32]

'Processes for tracking, responding to, and recovering from incidents and errors are followed and documented'; documented and exercised incident procedure. Communication to affected communities is outside the control. [AI 100-1 Table 4 p.33]
Monitoring plans include 'incident response, recovery'. [AI 100-1 Table 4 p.33]
'Contingency processes are in place to handle failures or incidents in third-party data or AI systems'; quarantine covers MCP servers and indexes. [AI 100-1 Table 1 p.24]
'Develop and update GAI system incident response and recovery plans and procedures'. [AI 600-1 p.41]

Third-party incident plans: 'Define ownership of GAI incident response functions; Rehearse third-party GAI incident response plans at a regular cadence'; E-08 requires an exercise per release cycle. [AI 600-1 p.22]
'after action reviews of GAI system incident response'; exercises feed procedure updates. [AI 600-1 p.16]
'Conduct after-action assessments for GAI system incidents to verify incident response and recovery processes are followed and effective'. [AI 600-1 p.45]

'Establish and maintain procedures for the remediation of issues which trigger incident response processes'; quarantine, purge by lineage, restore from a trusted baseline and approved reintegration under E-08 are such procedures. [AI 600-1 p.42]

E-09.justification: Post-deployment plans include 'change management'; E-09 versions security configuration and triages every change with an accountable approver. [AI 100-1 Table 4 p.33]
Effectiveness of existing controls is 'regularly assessed and updated'; mapped control tests re-run on change. [AI 100-1 Table 3 p.29]
'Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process'; capability-profile changes trigger full reassessment. [AI 100-1 Table 1 p.23]
Pre-trained model changes are handled as part of regular monitoring and maintenance. [AI 100-1 Table 4 p.32]

'Re-assess model risks after fine-tuning or retrieval-augmented generation implementation and for any third-party GAI models deployed for applications and/or use cases that were not evaluated in initial testing'. [AI 600-1 p.42]
'Regularly review security and safety guardrails, especially if the GAI system is being operated in novel circumstances'. [AI 600-1 p.31]

E-10.justification: Transparency and accountability risks are examined; tamper-evident storage makes the audit trail trustworthy. [AI 100-1 Table 3 p.30]
'Regularly assess and verify that security measures remain effective and have not been compromised'; scheduled integrity checks of the audit store. [AI 600-1 p.34]

aisvs.source_version: OWASP AISVS 1.0 (June 2026), locked 1.0/en folder at commit 94fbad5acee4e4716bff263a4c455dfd780e53a7
notes: Identifiers: AISVS requirements are cited in the version-prefixed form the AISVS README recommends, v1.0-C<chapter>.<section>.<requirement>. Appendix C (AI-assisted secure coding) items are cited by analogy as v1.0-AC.<section>.<item>; they are organizational controls for AI coding tools and are used mainly for coding-agent controls, otherwise only as supports.

Levels: in catalog/mappings.json, each justification starts with the AISVS level of the requirement. Several Level 1 controls here map to AISVS requirements at a higher AISVS level, for example A-04, A-11, A-23, I-04, I-06, I-13, I-18 and I-19. AISVS levels are assurance depths an organization selects (AISVS level N assumes ASVS level N in parallel), while this catalog's levels are computed from a capability profile, so neither substitutes for the other.

Unmapped on purpose: AISVS leaves governance, risk acceptance and risk management to ISO/IEC 42001 and NIST AI RMF (R-01 to R-03), does not define test-harness or evidence-scope methods (S-01, S-02, S-03, S-05), and leaves audit log custody to ASVS (E-02). No AISVS 1.0 requirement corresponds to idempotency, task-scope binding, approval fatigue, system-of-record reads, provider data routing or MCP sampling and elicitation (A-05, A-07, A-13, I-08, I-10, I-20).

Taint propagation (I-01), argument provenance (A-06) and Rule of Two gating (A-08) have no AISVS equivalent beyond the instruction-hierarchy and separation requirements cited, so those mappings are partial or supports.
Reuse boundary: justifications paraphrase AISVS in this project's own words; no AISVS requirement text is reproduced.

R-04.justification: AISVS L1. Requires an inventory of deployed model artifacts and their origin, which covers only the model-version slice of the R-04 inventory (not tools, MCP servers, recipients, boundary trace or ASI applicability).
Appendix C, L1. Requires a threat model per AI coding tool, agent or MCP server; this supports R-04 threat modeling for coding-agent contexts only.

R-05.justification: AISVS L2. Asks for a trusted reversibility class per high-impact action, matching the reversibility and consequence-class fields of the R-05 register but not trusted sources per argument or limits.
AISVS L2. Runtime must enforce those classifications, matching R-05's rule that the dispatcher reads policy from the register rather than from the model.
AISVS L2. Tool manifests declaring privileges and limits are a related form of trusted per-tool configuration, though without argument provenance.

R-06.justification: AISVS L3. Classification labels must follow data into embeddings, caches and outputs, one mechanism R-06's disclosure policy relies on; it does not require a per-class policy of permitted recipients, retention or most-restrictive defaulting.

A-01.justification: AISVS L2. Authorization decisions are made outside the model, in code or a policy engine; A-01 adds the single mandatory dispatch path across all entry points and adapters that nothing else can reach.
AISVS L2. Runtime-enforced fine-grained policy over tools and parameter values corresponds to the checks the A-01 dispatcher applies.
AISVS L2. Isolating the agent authorization decision point from the agent's execution environment supports A-01's requirement that model-influenced processes cannot bypass the dispatcher.
Appendix C, L2. Every privileged bot action routes through a separate audited authorization path decided by a policy engine, not the model; supports A-01's single dispatch path for coding bots.

A-02.justification: AISVS L1. Model output must be validated against a defined schema and rejected on mismatch; A-02 applies this to tool proposals and adds fail-closed policy errors and canonicalization.
AISVS L1. MCP servers must reject unknown or oversized parameters, matching A-02's rejection of fields a reviewed schema does not allow, for MCP only.
AISVS L2. Strict schema validation on MCP servers corresponds to A-02's strict-schema requirement within MCP scope.
AISVS L2. Default-deny allow-lists on AI resources support A-02's deny-by-default stance.

A-03.justification: AISVS L2. Keeping access decisions out of the model aligns with A-03's rule that model output cannot establish identity or authority.

AISVS L2. Propagating the user's integrity-protected authorization context to every downstream call matches A-03's requirement that the caller's permission, not a broad service credential, governs access.
AISVS L2. Per-invocation checks that the user's token authorizes the tool and its argument values correspond to A-03's per-call access check, for MCP servers.

A-04.justification: AISVS L3. Re-evaluating current backend policy on each privileged action in long sessions matches A-04's time-of-effect check; A-04 also covers queued and callback work and requires atomicity with the effect, and is Level 1 in the catalog.

A-06.justification: AISVS L2. Policies that restrict which parameter values an agent may supply support A-06, which further keys the check on taint and the argument's trusted source.
AISVS L2. Checking model-named external resources against an allow-list before invocation supports A-06's destination matching, without the normalization or provenance rules.

A-08.justification: AISVS L2. Isolating untrusted-data processing from tool calling corresponds to option (c) of A-08 (separation removes a property from the action-selecting context).
AISVS L1. Blocking high-impact actions until verified human approval corresponds to option (a) of A-08, though A-08 triggers on the three-property combination rather than on impact alone.

A-09.justification: AISVS L2. Runtime policy restricting which tools an agent may invoke corresponds to A-09's per-context tool profile.

AISVS L1. Per-tool sandboxing or isolation from model operations is execution isolation, closer to I-15; it supports A-09 but does not require limiting exposed operations, object types or a profile-scoped credential.
AISVS L1. Per-tool quotas including egress match A-09's per-tool rate and egress limits.
AISVS L2. Exposing only tools within authorized scopes in MCP tool listings supports A-09's minimal exposure.
AISVS L2. Runtime enforcement of privileges declared in tool manifests supports dispatcher enforcement of the profile.

A-10.justification: AISVS L1. Human approval before irreversible or high-impact actions matches A-10's approval branch; A-10 also accepts reversible-by-design as an alternative.
AISVS L2. Approval requests must show complete canonical parameters such as diffs, close to A-10's dry-run diff of the exact effect.
AISVS L2. Reversibility classification underpins which operations A-10 guards.
AISVS L2. Enforcing the classification by blocking or requiring approval supports A-10's gate.

A-11.justification: AISVS L3. Cryptographic binding of approvals to parameters, identity, context and a single-use nonce corresponds to A-11's binding; A-11 is Level 1, also allows trusted server-side storage, and adds approver re-check and transactional consumption.
AISVS L3. Keeping approval-issuing keys out of the agent runtime supports A-11's rule that approval claims from model-reachable sources are ignored.
AISVS L2. Blocking an action when approval is not given within the allowed time supports A-11's expiry binding.

A-12.justification: AISVS L2. Showing complete canonical parameters without truncation corresponds to A-12's canonical rendering; A-12 adds model-unwritable components, provenance per field and new-destination flags.

A-14.justification: AISVS L3, same level as A-14. Step-up authentication for high-risk operations, but its examples are platform operations rather than approvals of agent effects, and it has no dual-control element.
Appendix C, L1. Separation of requester and reviewer and exclusion of the AI agent as reviewer supports A-14's distinct-human, no-agent-approver rule, in the coding context.
Appendix C, L2. Two-person review for AI-modified security-critical files supports A-14's dual-control element in the coding context.

A-15.justification: AISVS L2. Inter-agent delegation must follow an explicit authorization policy; A-15 adds intersection semantics, envelope fields, depth limits and receiver re-authorization.
AISVS L2. A scope-limited, integrity-protected token carrying the user's context and enforced downstream corresponds to A-15's verified envelope tied to the initiating principal.
AISVS L3. Short-lived, minimally scoped signed tokens for agents across systems support A-15's expiring, audience-bound envelope.

A-16.justification: AISVS L2. Forbids MCP servers from forwarding client tokens downstream: A-16's no-passthrough rule, for MCP servers only. A-16 also requires audience-specific credentials, short-lived bound delegated credentials, session IDs that are not authentication and per-client consent at proxies.
AISVS L1. Checking issuer, audience, expiry and scope matches A-16's requirement that services reject tokens not issued for them.
AISVS L1. Per-request token validation, not relying on the transport, aligns with A-16's rule that a session identifier is not authentication.
AISVS L3. Short-lived minimal-scope tokens support A-16's short-lived delegated credentials.

A-17.justification: AISVS L2, same level as A-17. Each agent instance has its own cryptographic identity acting as a principal, matching A-17's distinct workload identity.
AISVS L2. Acting for a user through a scope-limited token carrying the user's context corresponds to A-17's on-behalf-of flow; A-17 also requires subject and actor to be recorded.
Appendix C, L2. Scoped non-human identities for AI systems support A-17 in the coding context.

A-18.justification: AISVS L3, same level as A-18. Requires mTLS or DPoP sender-constraint, but only for MCP client-server tokens; A-18 covers all agent and adapter tokens and ties lifetime to revocation latency.

A-19.justification: AISVS L2. Filters responses to what the requester may see; A-19 limits shared-context output to what every principal who can view it may see and adds trigger-sender and speaker-change rules, which per-requester filtering does not cover.
AISVS L1. Treating any input that can steer the model as untrusted supports A-19's rule that trigger senders are content, not principals (A-19 does not rely on classifiers).

A-20.justification: AISVS L1. Runtime-enforced per-execution budgets (depth, tokens, spend) correspond to A-20; A-20 adds shared accounting across descendants, fallbacks and retries.
AISVS L1. Per-tool quotas and timeouts support run-level limits.

A-21.justification: AISVS L1. Enforced per-tool timeouts relate to A-21's caller-enforced deadlines; A-21 adds bounded retries and no re-routing after denial.

A-22.justification: AISVS L1. Per-principal and global rate limits on inference endpoints correspond to A-22's per-principal quotas, though AISVS frames them against model extraction; no provider spend cap.
AISVS L2. Granular token-usage attribution per user and workspace supports per-principal and per-tenant quota accounting.

A-23.justification: AISVS L2. Self-modification (prompts, tool lists, parameters) must be bounded by enforceable limits; A-23 is Level 1, names more targets, covers self-replication and requires credential-scope enforcement.
AISVS L3. Isolating signing keys from the agent runtime supports A-23's orchestrator-signing rule.
Appendix C, L1. Platform-enforced rules stop an agent from approving, merging, signing or deploying its own output; supports A-23 for coding agents.
Appendix C, L2. Agents cannot bypass branch protection or required checks; supports A-23's protection of CI security gates.

Appendix C, L1. Bot system prompts and policy configuration are hash-pinned and cannot be changed from repository or user-controllable input; supports A-23's ban on the agent writing its own prompts and policies, for coding bots.

A-24.justification: AISVS L2. Model output must not trigger outbound requests; A-24 extends this to content the agent posts where a renderer outside the application fetches it, and adds a per-recipient data-class check.
AISVS L3. Checking outputs for hidden or encoded content in formatting and structured fields supports A-24's check of outbound bodies for data-carrying references.

A-25.justification: AISVS L1. Blocking high-impact actions until verified human approval supports A-25, which also requires verification through the destination on record or the new destination, and notice to the previous destination, for redirecting values.

I-01.justification: AISVS L2. An instruction hierarchy depends on the application keeping untrusted inputs out of system and developer roles, which I-01's data-position rule requires; the model-side precedence itself is only a signal under I-01, which adds taint propagation enforced by the application.

AISVS L1. Shares I-01's scope of treating model-steering input as untrusted, but its operative obligation is classifier screening, which I-01 allows only as an added signal, never as sole enforcement.
AISVS L2. Architectural separation of untrusted tool-output processing supports I-01's handling of tool results as data.
AISVS L2. Agent and tool outputs not written to trusted memory without validation supports I-01's rule that taint survives memory writes.
AISVS L1. Screening MCP results for indirect injection is an added signal consistent with I-01's treatment of MCP results as untrusted.

I-02.justification: AISVS L2. Components handling untrusted data must be isolated from tool-calling, which is the core of I-02; I-02 adds typed or opaque returns, plan immutability and recording in the profile.
AISVS L2. Architectural separation between untrusted tool-output processing and agent operations corresponds to I-02's requirement that the privileged context not receive raw untrusted text.

I-03.justification: AISVS L1. Normalizing input before tokenization corresponds to I-03's pre-model normalization; I-03 specifies which characters to strip or flag and adds a reviewer view.
AISVS L1. Detecting and mitigating encoding smuggling (including explicit marking) corresponds to I-03's handling of tag, bidi and zero-width characters.
AISVS L2. Checking non-text inputs for hidden or embedded content supports I-03's extraction of hidden document text and provenance of OCR and transcripts.

I-04.justification: AISVS L2. Secrets must not be in the model's observable context including system prompts, matching I-04's no-credentials rule; I-04 is Level 1 and also excludes other principals' data and prompt-only enforcement.
AISVS L2. Access decisions never made by the model corresponds to I-04's rule that prompt-only rules are guidance, not implemented controls.

I-05.justification: AISVS L2. Keeping credentials out of model context, prompts and tool parameters matches the first half of I-05; I-05 also bans ambient credentials in model-influenced processes.
AISVS L2. Isolating the policy decision point from the agent's execution environment corresponds to I-05's rule that model-influenced processes cannot reach enforcement components.
AISVS L3. Isolating approval key material from the agent runtime supports I-05 for the approval store.
Appendix C, L2. Bots without mounted secrets and with only ephemeral credentials support I-05 for coding agents.

I-06.justification: AISVS L2. Enforcing the end user's authorization at each retrieval and assembly stage corresponds to I-06's pre-context authorization; I-06 is Level 1 and adds cache keys, score leakage and deletion propagation.
AISVS L2. Scope constraints on retrieval operations correspond to I-06's permission filtering.
AISVS L1. Per-tenant uniqueness of vector identifiers and namespaces supports I-06's per-tenant indexes.
AISVS L3. Propagating classification labels to embeddings and prompt caches supports I-06's rule that derived stores apply the same permissions.

I-07.justification: AISVS L2. Agent and tool outputs must not enter trusted memory without source validation, matching I-07's untrusted-derived storage of tainted writes.
AISVS L2. Tagging ingested documents with source, writer identity and timestamp at write time matches part of I-07's per-entry provenance fields.
AISVS L2. Excluding expired vectors from retrieval corresponds to I-07's expiry requirement.
AISVS L3. Retaining but excluding quarantined content supports I-07's quarantine option on revocation.
AISVS L1. Per-tenant namespace separation supports I-07's tenant partitioning.
AISVS L2. Immutable metadata after first write supports trustworthy provenance and trust-class fields.

I-09.justification: AISVS L3. Integrity protection of agent state persisted between invocations supports I-09's server-held, session-bound conversation state.
AISVS L2. Preventing injection of reserved role tokens addresses the same role-spoofing risk that I-09 handles by rejecting client-supplied system, assistant and tool-result messages.

I-11.justification: AISVS L2. Allow-listing MCP servers supports I-11's requirement to configure allowlists for remote connectors; AISVS does not address provider-hosted tools as egress channels.

I-12.justification: Appendix C, L2. Egress for AI bots is denied by default and limited to listed destinations; corresponds to I-12 in the coding context only.
AISVS L2. Preventing model output from triggering outbound requests supports I-12's control of model-influenced network access.

I-13.justification: AISVS L2. Model output must not trigger outbound requests, which covers I-13's auto-loaded remote images and previews; I-13 is Level 1 and adds link handling and open-redirect exclusions.
AISVS L3. Checking outputs for hidden or encoded content in formatting and structured fields supports detection of exfiltration payloads in rendered output.

I-14.justification: Appendix C, L1. Free-form bot output is never executed as command, query or workflow step, matching I-14's no-implicit-execution rule for coding bots.
AISVS L1. Schema validation of model output supports I-14, which adds that schema validity is not permission; per-sink encoding is deferred by AISVS to ASVS.

I-15.justification: AISVS L1. Tools execute in a least-privilege sandbox, the core of I-15; I-15 specifies non-root, no ambient credentials, pinned image and default-deny network.
AISVS L1. Enforced CPU, memory, disk, egress and time quotas per tool correspond to I-15's supervisor-enforced resource limits.
AISVS L2. Checking model-named packages against an approved registry before install is I-24's obligation; it only supports I-15, which confines model-proposed installs and imports to the sandbox.

I-16.justification: AISVS L3. Hardware partitioning or dedicated allocation on shared compute supports I-16's stronger-than-container boundary; AISVS frames it for model serving and tenants, not code shaped by untrusted input.
AISVS L2. Preventing cross-workload influence on shared serving infrastructure supports I-16's no-reuse-across-sessions rule.

I-17.justification: AISVS L1. Least-privilege isolation of tools supports isolating the browser tool; AISVS has no browser or computer-use specific requirement.

I-18.justification: AISVS L3. Snapshotting tool definitions and requiring re-approval on change corresponds to I-18's pinning and disable-on-change; I-18 is Level 1 and adds qualified names and collision handling.
AISVS L2. Only allow-listed MCP servers may be used, matching I-18's refusal to load unpinned, uninventoried servers.
AISVS L1. Trusted sourcing and cryptographic verification of MCP components supports I-18, which notes that a signature identifies a publisher, not descriptor safety.
AISVS L1. Validating tool listings against declared schemas before they reach the model supports I-18's handling of descriptors.

I-19.justification: AISVS L2. Local MCP servers are sandboxed with least privilege, matching I-19's sandbox requirement; I-19 is Level 1 and adds exact-command approval and unwritable configuration files.
AISVS L2. Explicit user consent when installing a local MCP server corresponds to I-19's configuration-time approval of the launch command.
AISVS L1. Restricting stdio transport to controlled local environments supports I-19's confinement of stdio servers.
Appendix C, L1. Integrity-checked bot configuration not modifiable from repository content supports I-19's rule that files defining servers, tools, skills or rules are not agent-writable.

I-21.justification: AISVS L2. Signed MCP responses with nonce and timestamp for replay detection correspond to I-21's integrity, nonce and replay rejection, limited to MCP.
AISVS L1. Authenticated, encrypted transport for remote MCP corresponds to I-21's authentication and confidentiality requirements.
AISVS L2. Enforcing a minimum protocol version corresponds to I-21's pinned protocol version with downgrade rejection.
AISVS L2. Cryptographic binding of actions to each step of the chain supports run binding of inter-agent messages.
AISVS L2. Each agent instance has its own cryptographic identity and authenticates as a principal, which supports I-21's mutual authentication of inter-agent messages.

I-22.justification: AISVS L2, same level as I-22. Binding actions to each execution-chain step corresponds to I-22's lineage ID to the originating output.
AISVS L3. Automated containment on policy violations supports I-22's circuit breakers.
AISVS L3. Applying the highest-impact classification across multi-agent chains supports I-22's producer-independent gating before fan-out.

I-23.justification: Appendix C, L2. Zero-privilege, read-only mode for untrusted fork PRs corresponds to I-23's ban on write tokens and secrets on outsider-triggered events.
Appendix C, L1. All PR-supplied content is untrusted input, matching I-23's treatment of contributor content.
Appendix C, L1. Issues, comments, commit messages and external docs fed to AI tools are untrusted, matching I-23's untrusted repository content.
Appendix C, L2. Agents cannot bypass branch protection or required checks, matching I-23's ban on changing CI and branch protection without review.
Appendix C, L1. Bot prompts and policy config cannot be modified from repository or branch content, matching I-23's protection of the agent's own instruction files.
Appendix C, L2. Dual control on high-impact pipeline trigger configuration supports I-23's human review of CI workflow changes.

Appendix C, L1. Workflows triggered by untrusted contributions must not run untrusted code where repository write permissions or secrets are available. This is I-23's core ban on write tokens and secrets on outsider-triggered events, at the CI platform level.
Appendix C, L1. Secrets withheld from workflows running fork or first-time-contributor code unless a manual approval gate is passed; matches I-23's no-secrets-on-outsider-events rule.
Appendix C, L2. Workflow definition changes go through an elevated security review path that AI agents cannot bypass; matches I-23's ban on changing CI workflows without human review.
Appendix C, L1. Credentials and job tokens not persisted into workspaces processing fork-originated or AI-touched code; supports I-23 and I-05 for CI agents.

I-24.justification: AISVS L1. A registry of deployed model artifacts and origins corresponds to I-24's explicit model versions with recorded provenance; general dependency pinning is deferred by AISVS to SCVS and SLSA.
AISVS L2. Verifying model-named external resources against an approved registry before install matches I-24's check of model-proposed dependencies.
AISVS L1. Obtaining MCP components from trusted sources with cryptographic verification corresponds to I-24's pinning and provenance for MCP servers.
AISVS L3. Re-evaluation on provider model, version or routing change supports I-24's no-floating-alias rule.
Appendix C, L2. PR gates detect typosquatted or non-resolving dependency names; supports I-24's verification of model-proposed dependencies against an approved registry.

I-25.justification: AISVS L1. An allow-list of serialization formats that cannot execute code on load covers I-25's non-executable-format clause; hash verification and fine-tuning data provenance map to other requirements.
AISVS L2. Third-party model artifacts must be integrity-verifiable, corresponding to I-25's hash verification.
AISVS L1. Weights and adapters only from approved sources corresponds to I-25's recorded source.
AISVS L2. Inventory of training-data sources with origin and processing history corresponds to I-25's provenance tracking of fine-tuning data.
AISVS L2. Poisoning detection in fine-tuning pipelines corresponds to I-25's review of training data as a poisoning path.
AISVS L2. Signature verification at admission and load supports I-25's verified loading.

I-26.justification: AISVS L3. Checking outputs for misleading content via homoglyphs or formatting supports I-26's handling of deceptive agent requests; AISVS has no requirement on trusted credential collection or labeling agent suggestions.

I-27.justification: AISVS L3. Tenant isolation on shared compute via hardware partitioning or dedicated allocation supports I-27's rule that no kernel is shared across tenants; AISVS frames it for model serving, not agent-run code.
AISVS L2. Preventing cross-tenant influence on shared serving infrastructure supports I-27's fresh sandbox per tenant and session.

S-04.justification: AISVS L1. Evaluation against known adversarial techniques per modality supports S-04's injection coverage; S-04 additionally requires deterministic fixtures per channel through the real enforcement path.

S-06.justification: Appendix C, L2. Blocking merge on critical findings with a human-approved written exception supports S-06's release gate, in the coding context.

S-07.justification: AISVS L1. A version-controlled suite run on model updates, but for alignment behavior rather than security controls; it shares only the run-on-change pattern with S-07's control-keyed regression tests.
AISVS L3. Security re-evaluation on provider model, version or routing changes corresponds to S-07's trigger on model and provider changes.
Appendix C, L3. Regression runs after prompt changes or model upgrades with baseline gating support S-07 for coding tools.

S-08.justification: AISVS L1. Adversarial evaluation of models corresponds to S-08's live-model evaluation; S-08 is Level 2, targets the delivered application and specifies trial counts and metrics.
AISVS L2. A behavioral acceptance suite before promotion supports pre-release evaluation.
Appendix C, L2. Indirect-injection testing before onboarding and after model or prompt change supports S-08 for coding tools.

S-09.justification: Appendix C, L2. Scheduled red-team exercises against AI tooling with severity-tracked remediation support S-09; AISVS does not require reviewer independence or adaptive attacks.

S-10.justification: AISVS L3, same level as S-10. Re-evaluation before continued use after provider model or routing changes corresponds to S-10's pre-rollout check; S-10 specifies replay of recorded runs and blast-radius caps.
AISVS L2. Rollout with automated rollback triggers supports controlled rollout of changed configurations.

E-01.justification: AISVS L2. Forensic logging of policy decisions, scoped to content moderation; E-01's policy decisions are authorization and dispatch decisions with reason codes, so this is related practice only.
AISVS L2. Audit logs with approver identity, timestamp, parameters and outcome correspond to E-01's approval and effect events.
AISVS L1. Logging AI interactions with session context corresponds to E-01's correlation fields; E-01 adds proposal versus effect distinction and taint state.
AISVS L2. A structured interoperable schema with model and provider identifiers supports E-01's structured events.

E-03.justification: AISVS L2. Logging retrieval queries, documents and sources corresponds to the retrieved-document part of E-03's context manifest.
AISVS L2. Model identifier and provider in a structured schema support E-03's model-version references.
Appendix C, L1. Correlated prompt and response records enabling chain replay support E-03 for coding tools.

E-04.justification: AISVS L2. Logging kill-switch activations and overrides matches one signal in E-04's list; E-04 also requires routing to a named owner.
AISVS L1. Detection and alerting on injection attempts supports E-04's tainted-context denial signals, as detection supplementing enforcement.
Appendix C, L1. User flags of insecure suggestions tracked to closure support E-04's user-report signal in the coding context.

E-05.justification: AISVS L2, same level as E-05. Behavioral anomaly detection on unusual patterns and retries corresponds to E-05's baselining and alerting; E-05 targets tool sequences, destinations and fan-out.
AISVS L3. Automated tool containment on policy violation corresponds to E-05's automatic throttle or suspend at narrowest scope.
AISVS L3. Distinguishing unexplained behavioral shifts from expected drift supports E-05's threshold tuning.
AISVS L2. Autonomous action triggers include behavior-pattern analysis; supports E-05's baselining of agent behavior, without thresholds or automatic containment.

E-06.justification: AISVS L1, same level as E-06. A manual kill-switch that halts inference and output corresponds to E-06's stop; E-06 adds descendant runs, per-component disable and queued-work handling.
AISVS L3. Kill-switch through an out-of-band channel isolated from the agent supports stop-without-deploy reliability.

E-07.justification: AISVS L2, same level as E-07. A swarm-level kill-switch halting all agents corresponds to E-07's global scope; E-07 adds tenant scope, credential revocation and measured latency.
AISVS L3. Out-of-band kill-switch channel supports E-07's scoped stop controls.

Appendix C, L2 (same level as E-07). AI agent identities must be rapidly revocable with a written, periodically tested time-to-revoke target, which is close to E-07's stated and measured revocation latency, limited to the coding context and without tenant or global scopes.

E-08.justification: AISVS L2, same level as E-08. Ability to reset memory corresponds to E-08's purge and restore of a memory scope.
AISVS L3. Quarantine that retains but excludes content supports E-08's quarantine with evidence preservation.
AISVS L2. Rollback restoring complete model state supports E-08's restore from a trusted baseline.
AISVS L3. Automated tool containment supports E-08's quarantine of a suspect component.

Appendix C, L1. An incident playbook for AI-in-pipeline compromise covering credential revocation, artifact quarantine, notification and forensic preservation corresponds to E-08's documented incident procedure, in the coding context.
Appendix C, L3. Remediation is exercised in tabletop or live-fire drills at least yearly; supports E-08's requirement that the incident procedure be exercised (E-08 requires once per release cycle).

E-09.justification: AISVS L3. Security re-evaluation on provider, model or routing change corresponds to E-09's re-assessment for model and provider changes; E-09 also governs tools, permissions, budgets and prompts.
AISVS L2. Immutable audit records for model changes support E-09's recorded, approved changes.

E-10.justification: Appendix C, L3, same level as E-10. Tamper-evident (append-only or WORM) storage for AI event logs corresponds to E-10 in the coding context; scheduled integrity checks are not required.
AISVS L2. Immutable audit records, but only for model changes, support E-10's tamper evidence.
Appendix C, L2. Bot prompts, tool calls and outputs logged to tamper-evident storage; corresponds to E-10's tamper-evident audit for coding bots, without scheduled integrity checks.
